clue.text: Did he always take opposite' points of view ?

definitions.text: Did he always take opposite' points of view

parts.words: Did he always take opposite' points of view
parts.note: a figure with two faces looking in opposite directions literally sees both ways at once; the Roman god of doorways fits

explanation.surface: Someone asks about a person who always argued the contrary.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a contrarian; the cryptic reading is literal: the two-faced Roman god of gateways looks forwards and backwards at once.
explanation.definitionFit: The Roman god of doorways is shown with two faces gazing in opposite directions.

clue.text: Child's play, etc, bound /to "produce" them?

parts.note: plays and verses an author wrote as a child, later gathered and bound into a volume

explanation.surface: Children playing are sure to create things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Child's play' means a play written by a child; 'bound' means bound as a book, not certain.
explanation.definitionFit: The term covers works an author produced in youth.

clue.text: Material can be shaped only after cutting off either end

indicators.note: the letters can be shaped into a new arrangement
removing both outside letters of the word end leaves only its middle

explanation.surface: Cloth can only be cut to shape after its ends are trimmed off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can be shaped' rearranges ONLY to NYLO; 'cutting off either end' leaves N, the middle of END.
explanation.definitionFit: This synthetic fibre is used as a fabric for stockings and clothing.

clue.text: Legislators wise as Nestor'? Possibly

indicators.note: possibly signals that the letters could be arranged another way

explanation.surface: Lawmakers are perhaps as wise as the old Greek counsellor.
explanation.walkthrough: Nestor was the wise old king in Homer.
explanation.definitionFit: Members of a senate make laws.

clue.text: Outcome of appeal, when bail's not supported ?.

definitions.text: Outcome of appeal, when bail's not supported ?

parts.words: Outcome of appeal, when bail's not supported ?
parts.note: read as cricket: the fielders appeal to the umpire, and when a bail falls off the stumps the batsman is out

explanation.surface: A legal appeal fails and the court refuses to back a prisoner's bail.
explanation.walkthrough: The court-room words are cricket ones: an appeal is a shout to the umpire, and the bails are the small wooden pieces resting on the stumps, which fall when a batsman is bowled.
explanation.definitionFit: When a batsman is out, the umpire's ruling sends them off; a court can likewise throw out an appeal.

clue.text: Odd extracts from diaries for supporter of throne

indicators.note: taking the odd-numbered letters, first, third, fifth and seventh, extracts them from the word

explanation.surface: Strange passages from a royal diary.
explanation.definitionFit: A throne stands on a raised platform at the end of a hall.

clue.text: Monument gets replanned round a single layer

indicators.note: round means one lot of letters goes around the other
replanned means planned anew, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: a single means one
a hen is a bird that lays eggs

explanation.surface: An ancient monument is redesigned around a single stratum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'replanned' shuffles the first word, and 'round' wraps it about the rest; a layer is a laying hen, not a stratum, which is where the surface misleads.
explanation.definitionFit: This prehistoric stone circle on Salisbury Plain is a famous English monument.

clue.text: Is this book abbreviated?

parts.note: the short form of this Old Testament prophet's book is written Isa., which looks like the words is a

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a book has been shortened.
explanation.walkthrough: The abbreviation Isa. reads as 'Is a', echoing the start of the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: This Old Testament book of prophecy is abbreviated Isa.

clue.text: Keep up with the Joneses-in this National Park

definitions.text: Keep up with the Joneses-in this National Park

parts.words: Keep up with the Joneses-in this National Park
parts.note: Jones is a typical Welsh surname, and to keep up you climb the highest mountain in Wales

explanation.surface: Matching the neighbours' lifestyle in a protected landscape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Keep up with the Joneses' means match the neighbours; here it means climb with the Welsh, Jones being a typical Welsh surname.
explanation.definitionFit: This mountainous National Park in north Wales takes its name from Wales's highest peak.

clue.text: Scientific 'device, one not working, we hear.

indicators.note: we hear signals that the word is judged by its sound

parts.note: someone who lazes about does no work

explanation.surface: A piece of lab kit, one of them broken, so rumour says.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one not working' suggests a broken device; it is a lazer, an idler.
explanation.definitionFit: This device produces an intense narrow beam of light for science and industry.

clue.text: Film' star gave sweetheart endless love

indicators.note: the word for a sweetheart loses its final letter, so it has no end

parts.note: a valentine is a sweetheart chosen on 14 February
love is zero in tennis, written as the letter O

explanation.surface: A screen idol gave his darling a love that never ended.
explanation.walkthrough: Rudolph Valentino was the silent-film heart-throb of the 1920s.
explanation.definitionFit: Rudolph Valentino was a famous silent-screen actor.

clue.text: Drug, certain oxen after skinning them

indicators.note: to be in the buff is to be bare-skinned, so stripping off the buff skins the beasts

parts.note: buffaloes are a kind of wild ox

explanation.surface: A drug is extracted from particular cattle once they have been flayed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Skinning' removes BUFF, the old word for bare skin (in the buff = naked), from the front of BUFFALOES.
explanation.definitionFit: Bitter aloes is a purgative medicine made from the juice of aloe leaves.

clue.text: Score above the average in -vital innings

definitions.text: Score above the average in -vital innings

parts.words: Score above the average in -vital innings
parts.note: a batsman's tally that is well above par in an important cricket innings, just short of a century

explanation.surface: A batsman makes a better than average score when it really matters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Score' looks like a cricket score but is also twenty; a figure four and a half times a score is a big tally in an innings.
explanation.definitionFit: A cricketer who makes a tally ten short of a century has batted well above the average.

clue.text: Ill-mannered playwright

indicators.note: ill means badly, so the letters of the next word are treated badly and rearranged

explanation.surface: A rude dramatist.
explanation.definitionFit: Menander was a Greek comic dramatist of the fourth century BC.

clue.text: Broad and flat as a baby's brain at birth

parts.note: tabular means flat like a table top
taken as written

explanation.surface: A newborn's mind is broad and flat.
explanation.walkthrough: The Latin phrase means a scraped tablet, the idea that the mind starts with nothing written on it.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin for blank slate describes the mind before experience writes on it.

clue.text: Man with convictions an exception to the rule

definitions.meaning: a criminal with a record of court convictions, not a person of strong beliefs
someone who breaks the law is an exception to it in a punning sense

explanation.definitionFit: A criminal has convictions in court and, as one who flouts the law, is literally an exception to the rule.

clue.text: Yet this game may make player 'too wet.

indicators.note: may make says the letters of the phrase can be rearranged, together with another word, into something new

explanation.surface: A swimming-pool sport may leave a player drenched.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer's letters together with YET can be rearranged to make PLAYER TOO WET.
explanation.definitionFit: This team ball sport is played in a swimming pool.

clue.text: Card-game. played with matches

parts.note: a children's card game in which players shout when two cards turned up match, not one played for matchsticks

explanation.surface: A game of cards where the stakes are matchsticks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Matches' suggests matchsticks used as betting chips; it means pairs of cards that match.
explanation.definitionFit: In this children's game you call out when two cards of equal rank appear together.

clue.text: After mixing, let me pour 'precious liquid

indicators.note: after mixing signals that the letters are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone asks to pour a valuable drink once it is mixed.
explanation.definitionFit: Crude oil is a highly valued liquid, sometimes called black gold.

clue.text: Things are a bind to the trainee

definitions.meaning: a legal apprentice was bound by a contract of training to the firm

explanation.definitionFit: The word means items, and a trainee solicitor was once bound by a training contract.

clue.text: Cast turned inside-out revealing what it does

indicators.note: the inner pair of letters goes to the outside and the outer pair goes inside, a rearrangement

explanation.surface: A theatre cast shows its true colours once turned inside out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned inside-out' swaps CAST's middle AS to the outside and its outer C, T into the middle: A-CT-S.
explanation.definitionFit: A theatrical cast performs on stage, which is exactly its job.

clue.text: Nightingale and duck, say, for Krishna

indicators.note: say signals that the words only sound like the answer

parts.note: a jugger is a bird that sings jug-jug as the nightingale does, and a duck is nought in cricket

explanation.surface: Two birds, a songster and a waterfowl, are offered up for a Hindu god.
explanation.walkthrough: The nightingale's song was written 'jug-jug', so it is a jugger; a duck in cricket is a score of nought. Together they sound like the god's title.
explanation.definitionFit: Juggernaut, from Jagannath (lord of the world), is a title of Krishna as Vishnu's incarnation.

clue.text: Ship with. 60% less manpower than Nineveh's?

definitions.text: Ship with. 60% less manpower than Nineveh's?

parts.words: Ship with. 60% less manpower than Nineveh's?
parts.note: Masefield's quinquireme of Nineveh had five banks of oars; a galley with two banks has three-fifths fewer rowers

explanation.surface: A vessel needing far fewer crew than an ancient Assyrian ship.
explanation.walkthrough: Masefield's poem 'Cargoes' opens with the 'Quinquireme of Nineveh'; five banks of oars down to two is a 60% cut.
explanation.definitionFit: An ancient galley with two banks of oars.

clue.text: News broadcast makes all these points

definitions.text: News broadcast makes all these points

parts.words: News broadcast makes all these points
parts.note: the letters of news, spread around, stand for north, east, west and south, the main compass directions

explanation.surface: A news bulletin covers every one of these topics.
explanation.walkthrough: N, E, W, S are the four main compass points; 'broadcast' means scattered.
explanation.definitionFit: North, south, east and west are called the cardinal points of the compass.

clue.text: For him the heart of the. message comes last

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its central letter
comes last says the central letter is moved to the very end of the word

parts.note: a cable is a telegram message

explanation.surface: For one man, the key part of the letter is saved for the end.
explanation.walkthrough: The middle letter B of CABLE moves to the end. Caleb was one of the spies Moses sent into Canaan.
explanation.definitionFit: Caleb is a biblical man's name, so a fitting stand-in for 'him'.

clue.text: Artist arrived at about one

indicators.note: about means around, so one phrase wraps around the other

parts.note: to arrive at a place is to get to it
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A painter reaches a destination around one o'clock.
explanation.definitionFit: Giotto was an early Italian Renaissance painter.

clue.text: Nobleman from 18--one interrupting another

indicators.note: interrupting means breaking into the middle of the other word

parts.note: another article, the definite one, from 18 (articles)
one article from 18: the indefinite one

explanation.surface: A lord breaks into another conversation.
explanation.walkthrough: '18' points to the answer of 18 down, articles: the indefinite one goes 'interrupting', inside the definite one.
explanation.definitionFit: A thane was an Anglo-Saxon or Scottish lord holding land from the king.

clue.text: Eager to split difference between giant pair

indicators.note: the two giants' names differ by two letters; splitting that difference removes one of them

parts.note: Gog and Magog are a legendary pair of giants guarding the City of London

explanation.surface: Keen to compromise between two huge figures.
explanation.walkthrough: MAGOG differs from GOG by MA; splitting that difference adds just A to GOG, i.e. MAGOG loses its M.
explanation.definitionFit: To be all keyed up and excited is to be keen.

clue.text: Discharge last of brigade 'after battle

indicators.note: after puts the brigade's final letter behind the battle

parts.note: Loos was a First World War battle in France in 1915

indicators.note: last of picks the final letter of the word brigade

explanation.surface: A brigade's rear guard is demobilised once the battle is over.
explanation.definitionFit: To loose an arrow or gun is to fire it off, a synonym of discharge.

clue.text: It's no pie in the sky we enjoy a slice of

definitions.text: It's no pie in the sky we enjoy a slice of

parts.words: It's no pie in the sky we enjoy a slice of
parts.note: something heavenly yet real that we eat in slices: a light sponge named after celestial beings

explanation.surface: A real treat, not an empty promise, which we enjoy a portion of.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pie in the sky' means an empty promise; this heavenly-named sponge is real and sliceable.
explanation.definitionFit: This light white sponge is named for heavenly beings yet is a solid treat to slice.

clue.text: Outback "object.

parts.note: a thrown thing from the Australian bush that comes back to the thrower, out and back

explanation.surface: An item from the Australian bush.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outback' is the Australian bush but also suggests something that goes out and comes back.
explanation.definitionFit: This curved Aboriginal throwing stick returns to the thrower and is iconic of Australia.

clue.text: Rocket' propellant

parts.note: Rocket was Stephenson's early railway locomotive, driven by boiler vapour rather than rocket fuel

explanation.surface: Fuel for a rocket.
explanation.walkthrough: Not a space rocket: Stephenson's Rocket of 1829 was a pioneering locomotive.
explanation.definitionFit: Stephenson's Rocket locomotive was driven by water vapour from its boiler.
